explanation: The basic sentence. は marks the topic and is pronounced "wa" here. です ends a polite statement.
Add か to the end of a polite sentence to make a question. No question-word order change, and no "?" needed.
の links two nouns. The owner or description comes first.
も replaces は or が and means "also".
これ is near the speaker, それ is near the listener, あれ is far from both.
The polite negative of です. In casual speech it becomes じゃない.
Japanese verbs come at the end of the sentence. ます covers both "do" and "will do".
Swap ます for ません to say "don't" or "won't".
を shows what the verb acts on. It is pronounced "o" and written wo in many typing systems.
に marks a destination and a specific time.
で marks where an action happens or the tool used to do it.
translation: I read a book at home.

explanation: へ marks a direction. It is pronounced "e". It often overlaps with に.
Swap ます for ました for the past.
Add でした to ません.
Swap ます for ましょう to suggest doing something together.
い adjectives go straight in front of a noun, and can end a sentence with です.
な adjectives take な before a noun, and です to end a sentence.
Change the final い to くない. Note that いい becomes よくない.

pattern: Aが あります／います
explanation: あります is for objects and います is for living things. が marks the thing that exists.

pattern: Bに Aが あります
explanation: Location comes first, marked by に.
translation: There is a shop at the station.

explanation: Use this to ask for an item.
Te form plus ください asks someone to do something.
After a place or time it means "from". After a sentence it gives a reason.
Marks the end of a range of time or space.
Swap ます for たい. Used for your own wishes.
translation: I want to go to Japan.
